summary: Markets closed at swing low after Nifty -270 and Bank Nifty -660 for the week; ICICI results reaction, OI map (put 10,000/call 11,000) and Nov range 9,500-10,500 proposed; 9,951 (March low) named as the line in the sand.

events.claim: Week before: Nifty lost ~270 points and Bank Nifty ~660 points; close at swing low (late Oct 2018)
ICICI Bank Q2 results: profit lower due to higher provisions, NIM improved; ICICI ADR rose ~4.8% in US Friday
Prior correction (Feb-Mar 2018) low was 9,951 on Nifty; speaker says market historically does not fall below previous correction low

lessons: Rallies on heavyweights: ADR read-through (ICICI +4.8% in US) signals ~200 pts Bank Nifty contribution next day.
Have a hard invalidation level (previous correction low) and exit all bullish bets below it.
quote: In every correction the markets did not fall below the previous corrections low. The March low was 9,951. If Nifty falls below 9,951 all my bullish bets are out.
leaks: "And thank you for watching The Last Street Week Ahead Program" (channel outro)

summary: First-ever Week Ahead video: 3-session COVID holiday week; India VIX falling; Friday's terrible US jobs data moved Dow only -300 (selling exhaustion); HDFC/ICICI ADRs -8% warn of weak Tuesday open; range 7,500-8,500.

events.claim: US non-farm payroll data was very bad but Dow fell only ~300 points (early April 2020), signalling selling exhaustion after weeks of 1,000+ point days
HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank ADRs fell ~8% and Infosys ADR ~4% in US trade before the Indian holiday week
India VIX was falling into the holiday-shortened week (3 trading sessions; Monday and Friday holidays)

lessons: When bad news moves markets less and less, selling is exhausting - negative impact is limited.
ADR moves of index heavyweights preview Indian bank stocks after holidays.
quote: All over the world, there seems to be some kind of selling exhaustion. So the impact on negative news is very limited.

summary: Nifty shot up ~10% in one day and decisively broke 8,500; FIIs bought 2,000+ crore after $10B+ selling (game changer); data calendar ahead; VIX ~50 so option buying discouraged; 8,000-10,000 OI range.

events.claim: Nifty rose nearly 10% in a single day and decisively broke the 8,500 level (week of 6-9 Apr 2020)
After relentless selling of more than $10 billion, FIIs bought over 2,000 crore in two sessions - called a game changer
India VIX around 50, far above US VIX; option buying discouraged
Rally of >20% from ~7,500 low meets the US definition of a bull market

lessons: After months of heavy FII selling, the first sustained FII buying is a regime signal.
When VIX is extremely high, sell options rather than buy - falling volatility eats premiums.
quote: Rising more than 20% from the low point is considered as a bull market by U.S. definition.

summary: Post-breakout consolidation 8,800-9,350; RBI announcement day saw Bank Nifty crash then surge (private bank index +7%, Axis +15%); PCR 0.88-0.9 = oversold despite 20% rally; 9,000-10,000 OI range; pent-up auto demand thesis.

events.claim: On RBI announcement day, Bank Nifty first fell then private sector bank index shot up more than 7%, Axis Bank +15%, ICICI Bank +10%
TCS came with excellent results and shot up 6%; Infosys results due Monday
HDFC Bank results slightly below street expectation (Q4 FY20, COVID quarter)
After Wuhan lockdown lifted, auto sales shot up - cited as template for Indian pent-up car demand

lessons: Put-call ratio ~0.9 after a 20% rally means still oversold - room for short covering, not top.
The more times a level (38.2% Fib ~9,300) is tested, the higher the odds of breakout.
quote: If the put call ratio is below 0.9 we can say markets are in oversold condition... despite such a fantastic rise of more than 20 percent markets are not in overbought condition.

summary: Historic week recap: WTI crude settled at -$37; Facebook invested ~45,000 crore in Jio (Reliance +10%); Gilead drug news lifted Monday to 9,384; PM stimulus meeting produced nothing; range 9,000-9,500 with resistance 9,300-9,400.

events.claim: US crude oil prices fell to zero and then to minus $37 (WTI May contract, 20 April 2020)
Facebook announced investment of ~45,000 crore (US$5.7bn) in Reliance Jio; Reliance shot up ~10% next day
Gilead coronavirus drug news lifted Nifty to a 9,384 high on Monday (20 April 2020)
PM meeting with financial officials on Friday ended without expected stimulus announcement (24-25 Apr 2020)

lessons: A single mega-news (Jio-Facebook) can lift the whole index via its heavyweight.
Known, expected events (PM stimulus) that don't materialize lead to consolidation, not crash.
quote: Nobody could have imagined that the crude prices fell to zero, not only zero, it fell minus $37.

summary: April series ended near highs (~9,850) but weekend brought lockdown extension and zero April auto sales; SGX indicated 500-650 point gap down (worst since March); monthly OI range 9,000-10,500; 10,000 major resistance (Fib 50%).

events.claim: India extended lockdown another two weeks; passenger vehicle companies declared zero sales for April
Reliance announced rights issue at 1,257 rupees - cited as a hangover for the stock
India manufacturing PMI expected ~41 after ~51 the previous month (April lockdown)
SGX Nifty indicated a 500-650 point gap-down for Monday - worst since March 2020

lessons: May is historically a weak month for equities ('Sell in May') - factor seasonality into OI positioning.
Known-bad data (zero auto sales) is priced in; markets react to surprises, not confirmations.
quote: Generally May month is a weak month for equities... in US they say sell everything in May and go away.

summary: Range call 9,000-9,500 validated exactly; ICICI Q4 profit ~2,000 crore vs ~3,500 crore expected (big miss); banks pressured by moratorium-extension news; NASDAQ turned positive for the year; consolidation must resolve - expecting breakout.

events.claim: ICICI Bank declared results Saturday: profit below 2,000 crore versus analyst expectation ~3,500 crore
Banks seeking three more months of loan moratorium pressured banking stocks (May 2020)
NASDAQ turned positive for the year on Friday (8 May 2020)
Nifty had consolidated between 9,000-9,500 for two weeks; 9,420 crossing expected to trigger short covering toward 10,000

lessons: Three weeks of tightening consolidation means a resolution move is near - prepare for either side.
Sell puts on intraday falls in a range with supportive OI; skip the call side when upside is capped.
quote: This consolidation cannot go on for a very long time. Sooner or later the markets will either break out or break down.

summary: ₹20 lakh crore package spiked hopes then sold off; FIIs accelerated selling (>2,000 crore Friday; >15,000 crore in 3 weeks); heavyweight banks fell 10-20% in May (Kotak -20%); VIX falling and PCR 0.8 say bottom near; range 9,000-9,500.

events.claim: Prime Minister announced economic package of 20 lakh crore on Tuesday evening; SGX spiked but market sold off at open
FIIs sold more than 15,000 crore in three weeks of May; Friday alone >2,000 crore in cash market
Kotak Bank fell nearly 20% in May; ICICI, Axis, HDFC Bank fell 10-20% in the month; Bank Nifty 22,000 -> 18,800
US stopped shipments to Huawei; US-China trade tension reappearing (mid-May 2020)

lessons: Falling VIX in a falling market means the remaining downside is limited.
PCR ~0.8 + put OI close to spot + call OI far away = sellers confident, bottom-building pattern.
quote: Despite market falling so much, India VIX keeps going down... the further fall from here may not be very big.

summary: Markets disappointed by 20-lakh-crore package details, tested 8,800 then recovered to 9,000-9,500; Bank Nifty 22,000->17,000 (-5,000 in 3 weeks, extremely oversold); expecting 250-300 point expiry-week move either side.

events.claim: Bank Nifty fell from ~22,000 to ~17,000 in three weeks of May 2020 - an extraordinary ~5,000-point fall
FIIs sold more than 15,000 crore in May (excluding block deals); bought large quantities only on two block-deal days
India-China border tension cited as an under-reported headwind (May 2020)
FIIs cut short positions and added longs in F&O towards end of last week

lessons: Extreme oversold conditions in Bank Nifty mean short covering can add ~300 Nifty points instantly.
In volatile expiry weeks, expect a 250-300 point move without confidently predicting direction.
quote: Bank Nifty is looking extremely oversold... in case there is any short covering, Bank Nifty can easily shoot up 1,000 points.

summary: Bank Nifty shot up ~2,400 points vindicating oversold call; Nifty expired 9,490; bear cases (China, GDP fear, zero auto sales, virus, border) systematically rebutted; FIIs turned buyers last 2 sessions; June target 10,000-10,200.

events.claim: Bank Nifty shot up nearly 2,400 points in the last week of May 2020; Nifty expired near 9,490
India GDP data (Jan-Mar 2020 quarter) came above 3% when many expected negative/1-2%
FIIs turned net buyers in the last two trading sessions of May after selling 15,000+ crore during the month
Government announced phased reopening of the economy from June 8

lessons: Markets worry about lead indicators (reopening), not lag indicators (GDP).
Known news (zero auto sales) is already priced - markets react only to surprises (efficient market hypothesis).
When FIIs turn buyers after a long selling streak, Nifty typically adds ~1,000 points.
quote: Markets will always worry about the lead indicator, not the lag indicator.

summary: Bullish call vindicated: Nifty 9,000->10,200 in ~7 sessions as FIIs turned daily buyers; US May payrolls +2.5M vs -8M expected sent Nasdaq to ATH; recounts Nov-2018 elections->Balakot FII cycle; NSE option-price glitch Thursday hurt traders.

events.claim: US May non-farm payrolls came +2,509K versus expected -8,000K; US markets shot up, Nasdaq at all-time high (5 June 2020)
NSE option prices malfunctioned on Thursday (4 June 2020); brokers stopped market orders; many traders lost money
Nifty rallied from ~9,000 (27 May) to ~10,200 (5 June) in about 7-8 trading sessions
Historical pattern: BJP lost 5 state elections Nov 21 2018 -> FII selling until Feb 26 2019 Balakot air strike -> FII buying and 1,000-point rally in March 2019 series

lessons: Don't be a bull or a bear - be a chameleon; markets change trend when everyone leans one way.
Always trade with the trend; fighting it with leverage (F&O) makes losses heavy.
quote: Do not be a bull, do not be a bear, be a chameleon - change the color as and when required.

summary: Nifty tested the 10,200 resistance then held 10,000 close-to-close; US jobs shock (+2M expected -8M) later corrected by BLS error (~5M misclassification); China trade beat ($62B surplus); Titan/Hero MotoCorp results week; range 9,700-10,350.

events.claim: US government corrected an error of almost 5 million jobs in the May jobs report - effectively about -3M instead of +2M, still better than -8M expected
China May trade data: trade balance $62B vs $39B expected; exports fell only 3.3% vs -7% expected
SGX Nifty tested 10,350 (100-day moving average) on Monday morning
Reliance and ITC helped Nifty hold above 10,000 on close-to-close basis despite intraday breaks

lessons: Highest put OI at a far strike can be stale profit positions - use second-highest OI for the live range.
Old major resistance (9,900-10,000) becomes major support on retests.
quote: You are the last one to know anything in this country... that data is already factored in the prices.

summary: US reality-check week: Nasdaq ATH despite 2M+ infections; Fed caution sent US -7% Thursday; Nifty closed ~10,000 Friday instead of feared crash (already -2% Thursday; Asia only -1-2%); IIP -55% (lockdown); consolidation 9,500-10,500.

India May IIP fell 55% and food inflation was +9.5% (full CPI not released due to COVID data collection issues)

Nifty fell from 10,350 to 9,700 within the week then recovered to ~10,000

lessons: Relative positioning logic: if you already fell 2% and Asia only falls 1-2% after a US -7% night, the gap-down gets bought.
Already-corrected markets have less downside from a global shock - fresh shorting invites short covering.
quote: Why should we fall 7%? ... In the morning many people would have shorted and all those people had to cover the short.

events.claim: India-China border tension news on Tuesday dropped Nifty to 9,700 before recovery (week of 15-19 June 2020)
PM speech misinterpreted by markets: Nifty fell ~150 points within half an hour; next day's speech sparked recovery
Reliance Industries announced it had become net-debt-free after investor fund raises; Jio and Retail public issues planned within 5 years; stock 875 (March) to 1,685 (Friday high)
FIIs turned net buyers Friday, buying more than 1,000 crore

lessons: Speech-driven drops are misinterpretations until proven otherwise - recoveries follow clarifications.
Watch marginal OI additions (10,000 put) rather than stale max OI for the live support.
quote: Reliance Industries has become the star of the week... almost doubled in the last two months.

summary: Post-rally consolidation view: support 9,900, resistance 10,700; Fed restricted bank buybacks (Dow -700 Friday); ITC results in line; data week ahead (auto sales, China/India PMI, US payrolls Thursday).

ITC results (Saturday) came in line with expectations
US economists polled expected ~3 million jobs added in June payrolls (released Thursday July 2 due to holiday)

lessons: After a 1,000-point monthly rally, expect 1-2 weeks of range consolidation, not continuation.
Central-bank restrictions on one sector (bank buybacks) can drag the whole US tape overnight.
quote: I am expecting Nifty to take support at 9,900 for the next week and expecting some resistance at 10,700.

summary: US jobs beats lifted Nifty to a 4-month high ~10,605; volatility regime shift - India VIX 30->25 and Friday's range <100 points (first in months); +55 points but calls didn't gain even 1 rupee; OI range 10,000-11,000.

India VIX fell from ~30 to ~25; Friday's Nifty high-low range was under 100 points, first time in 2-3 months

lessons: Falling VIX crushes premiums even on up days - option sellers win in quiet drifts.
OI map (max put 10,000, max call 11,000) with >90 premiums frames a clean range to sell around.
quote: Nifty was up by 55 points, but yet all the call options did not even go up by one rupee.

Reliance fell more than 120 rupees from highs post-results; holds ~16% weight in Nifty

lessons: A heavyweight insider sale can cost the index 1,000 points on one stock - weightage math matters.
